objective: Expose the existing bounded EvoIR program interpreter as a useful C undefined-behavior checker without changing interpreter or lowering semantics.
observed_gaps: The driver has --interpret-evoir, but no --check product command.
Diagnostics are rendered only as human-readable stderr lines.
No --explain command or tests/ui blessed-output suite exists.
The EvoIR driver currently reports runtime findings at input:1:1 because the executable IR has no source-span mapping; the product must not present that fallback as a precise runtime location.
The normative section 6.3 table does not cover every diagnostic named elsewhere in the specification or compiler; missing explanations must remain explicit TODOs.

interface.execution: Use the existing EvoIR main-contract validation and interpret_program path with its existing 100000-step limit and program lifecycle. Do not bypass unsupported external calls or convert fuel exhaustion to a successful check.
interface.success: Exit 0 means the admitted, executed path completed without a finding; it is not whole-program absence-of-UB proof. A nonzero C main result alone is not a checker finding. Report the main result separately from checker status.
interface.failure: Existing numbered diagnostics remain authoritative. Resource exhaustion and unsupported execution are failures to complete the check, not evidence of C UB and not PASS.
interface.explain: evocc --explain E3xxx; descriptions are derived from the exact section 6.3 table, including withdrawn/retired status. Codes known to the source/spec but missing that table receive an explicit explanation TODO; unknown codes are rejected.
interface.json: --error-format=json produces one valid JSON object per diagnostic on stderr, with a stable schema version, code (nullable for driver usage errors), message, severity, phase/category, source location when actually known, and explanation availability. Check completion is a separate structured stdout record. Existing modes retain their current stdout protocol.
interface.compatibility: Default human diagnostics and all existing CLI modes remain byte-compatible except the new opt-in interfaces. --check is mutually exclusive with existing action modes. JSON strings preserve Unicode and escape control characters.

red_cases: A defined program and a defined program returning nonzero complete successfully through --check.
Integer division by zero, uninitialized read, signed overflow, invalid shift, and out-of-bounds access retain existing E-codes.
An unresolved external call and fuel exhaustion are incomplete checks rather than successful or UB-free verdicts.
Lexer/preprocessor/parser errors use JSON when requested, including escaped paths and messages, and survey mode emits independently parseable records.
Runtime JSON locations are null/unavailable rather than fabricated 1:1 spans; front-end real spans remain present.
Every section 6.3 row has a generated explanation; every discovered named code outside it has an explicit TODO entry; retired/withdrawn annotations survive.
Unknown explain code, invalid error format, duplicate/conflicting modes, and missing input fail predictably.
Blessed text stderr fixtures cover representative runtime, front-end, unsupported, and resource outcomes; blessing is explicit, never automatic during tests.
Legacy --interpret-evoir output and diagnostics remain unchanged on the same fixtures.

owned: crates/evocc/build.rs (if needed for spec-derived diagnostic catalogue)
coordinated: crates/evocc/src/main.rs: narrowly scoped option/dispatch/diagnostic integration, coordinated with N02
crates/evocc/Cargo.toml: only if a small existing workspace dependency is necessary
forbidden: Interpreter semantics, limits, external-call behavior, or UB rules
EvoIR/EvoMIR semantic changes, P0/g0 registries, proof checker changes
New audit layer, capture identity layer, benchmark framework, or native campaign

focused: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/frontend CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo test --offline -p evocc --test check_product
Existing evocc diagnostic and interpreter integration tests
acceptance: python3 tools/render-status.py --todo after the TODO update
validation.lean: NOT_REQUIRED: no Lean or registry changes
validation.execution_owner: Root agent serializes all Cargo invocations; this lane does not launch Cargo independently.
metrics: JSON records validated and legacy-compatibility cases
Authoritative explanations and explicit explanation TODO counts

resources.retention: Keep only small UI fixtures, contract, compact receipt and one-page note. Remove test temporary outputs; no raw captures in Git, no new target or workspace tree.

stop_rule: Stop for semantic authority changes, a published-default regression that cannot be reverted within the slice, exhausted safe disk cleanup below 15 GiB, or deletion of sole open-task evidence. Otherwise record bounded gaps honestly and continue the authorized work.
claim_ceiling: Product access to existing interpreter diagnostics on executed, supported paths. Neither static whole-program analysis, complete libc/pthread execution, native sanitizer equivalence, nor absence-of-UB proof.
